text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Debt was kicked lower in late session trading by stronger than expected U.S. economic data and dealers said the next days' direction would largely depend on the U.S. market's close. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.78, down 0.42 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures weakened in line with Treasuries following stronger than expected U.S. November housing starts data. Volume was thin as the market appeared to be settling into pre-holiday lethargy. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-23/32, down 11/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures drifted lower in a lacklustre session in which declines in U.S. bond prices undermined the positive impact of the eleventh cut in the French intervention rate this year. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.34, down 0.14 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bond futures slipped lower by late afternoon in line with many other global bond markets following stronger than expected U.S. housing data and some caution ahead of Italian CPI data later this week. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.30, down 0.63 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were sharply lower in moderate midday trade as a stronger-than-expected housing starts report for November triggered a strong selloff across the yield curve. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-3/32, down 21/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.68 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended the Tokyo session higher. There was no particular news that encouraged buying, but the March contract closed up 0.32 at 125.62 amid an absence of sellers. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 125.51, up 0.21 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The seasonally quiet primary market was handed a novelty when EBRD set a jumbo five-year drachma FRN. The 40 billion drachma deal, with a Christmas Eve paydate, was launched to beat New Year tax changes. Other activity saw IFC launch a 100 million rand two-year bond, Credit Local set a 100 million Ecu bond, Dresdner Bank add 500 million French francs to a 12-year bond and KfW add 4.0 billion pesetas to a 20-year bond.
